title: aciphylla procumbens
intro: Aciphylla procumbens, commonly known as New Zealand spinach tree or tree parsley, is a plant species that belongs to the carrot family (Apiaceae). It has been traditionally used in Maori medicine to treat various health issues, including fever, rheumatism, and digestive problems. The plant is rich in bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, coumarins, and phenolic acids, which have been reported to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, contributing to its therapeutic actions such as wound healing and immune system support. The bioactive constituents of Aciphylla procumbens, including flavonoids and coumarins, may also contribute to its potential health benefits, including anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory effects.
